description: Fetch top-N result pages via the HTTP-first fetch stack (escalating per-URL to a browser-automation-studio capture), extract readable text, and produce a single-pass cited synthesis, exposed as discrete API endpoints and agent tools.

requirements.description: Fetch the top-N result page URLs from a prior L0 search via the L2 fetch stack (plain HTTP first, per-URL escalation to a browser-automation-studio capture for JS-shell pages), extract readable body text (stripping navigation, ads, boilerplate), and produce a single-pass cited synthesis using the LLM over the extracted content. Expose this capability as discrete API endpoints and as agent tool definitions consumable by the L3 agent. Fetched page content must not be stored as findings (auto-capture is opt-in for L2).
requirements.title: L2 Page Fetch, Text Extraction, and Single-Pass Cited Synthesis

validation.notes: Text extraction strips known boilerplate patterns (nav, footer, cookie banners) from a set of HTML fixtures and returns only body content
Text extraction returns a non-empty string for at least 90% of real-world article HTML fixtures
Synthesis output from L2 contains inline citations referencing only URLs from the fetched page set (no hallucinated sources)
HTTP fetch leg: status/content-type gating, body-size capping, redirect following, and readable-text extraction pinned against a live httptest server

Escalation decision matrix: good HTTP content never escalates; HTTP failure or thin (JS-shell) content escalates to the browser leg; browser-leg failure degrades to the HTTP result; no browser leg means HTTP-only
Browser escalation leg drives browser-automation-studio CaptureService.Capture with inline_dom=true (no artifact-path/filesystem coupling) and extracts readable text from the returned DOM

NON-HERMETIC live smoke: the production HTTP fetch leg retrieves a real public URL and extracts non-empty text (lesson from the 2026-06 browserless route-mismatch bug that seam tests could not catch); skip-guarded for offline/-short runs

L2 API endpoint schema validation: request must include query (empty -> InvalidArgument) and top_n clamped into 1..10; response includes synthesis text, citations array, the per-document excerpts actually sent to the model (excerpts field, transport-capped), and abstain_reason on abstention [the 'raw extracted excerpts' response field landed 2026-06-10 with the L2 observability pass: proto DocumentExcerpt + abstain_reason on RunL2Response]
Issue an L2 request for a known query, verify the fetch stack fetches exactly N pages, text extraction produces non-empty content for each, and synthesis output contains citations
Verify fetched page content is NOT persisted as findings in the database when capture flag is absent (opt-out default for L2)
L2 fetch + extract + synthesize for top-5 pages must complete within 15 seconds at p95 under normal network conditions
A developer or agent can invoke the L2 endpoint and receive a cited synthesis grounded in full page content, not just snippets
L2 results are richer than L1 but incur higher latency — the tradeoff is documented in the API

title: L2 Fetch, Read, and Synthesize
